panels.rationale: MAG3 renal scintigraphy of the infant shows no perceptible renal activity in either renal fossa, directly demonstrating absent functioning renal tissue and confirming the article's diagnosis of bilateral renal agenesis. Only soft tissue/blood pool activity is seen. The panel is a real patient image (nuclear medicine study), though the modality fits best under 'other' rather than the vocabulary's listed modalities.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Fetal sagittal ultrasound shows segmental anterior deviation of the abdominal aorta, described in the article as a sonographic marker of bilateral renal agenesis; autopsy confirmed bilateral renal agenesis. The sign is not in the provided finding vocabulary, so it is proposed. B: Color Doppler fetal ultrasound shows the abdominal aorta and labeled adrenal gland, illustrating the reported segmental anterior aortic deviation marker in prenatally diagnosed bilateral renal agenesis. The key finding is not in the provided vocabulary, so it is proposed.

panels.figure_caption: Sagittal view. (A) Deviation anterior to the abdominal aorta at T11-L1 level. (B) Color Doppler image.
in_text_mentions: Also, by sagittal imaging, we observed segmental anterior deviation in the aorta between T11 and L1 in the fetal abdominal aorta, at the level where the celiac trunk originated (Figure 2A, B). Fetal biometry was observed compatible with 18 weeks. After termination, at autopsy of the fetus, the kidneys were not found in the bilateral renal fossa (Figure 3A, B, C). It was observed that the structure, which was thought to be the adrenal gland macroscopically, filled the renal fossa in a rectangular shape. It was observed that both adrenal glands’ upper ends extended towards the back of the aorta
